rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4 (System Application and Verification) and Table 2 report the authors' own deployment of a ZigBee wireless sensor network with a fuzzy controller on three drip-irrigated plots in Mahoba District, Uttar Pradesh, with 40 readings of weather inputs and valve-opening percentages taken March-September 2023, plus communication bit-error measurements at 250 m node distance.
rows.notes: The study is a system-design and field-deployment paper. What it actually shows is that the fuzzy-controlled valves operated and communication was reliable (bit error rate under 2.2% at 250 m); Table 2 lists only weather inputs and valve-opening percentages. The sole statement on water saving is a single sentence that the system 'claims to save 10% water compared to a traditional irrigation system', with no measured water volumes, no control/traditional treatment, and no comparison data reported; the authors' own wording is a claim rather than a measured result, so it is not counted as own evidence on water conservation. Note also that the review attributes a central value of ~40% water saving to this study, whereas the paper states 10%. The functioning of the controller is at best a precondition for the claimed water saving (upstream). The test was on drip irrigation despite the title referring to a sprinkler controller, but the technology (sensor-based smart controller) matches the claim, so no technology mismatch is flagged.

notes: Short conference proceeding paper (Eng. Proc. 2024). Full text appears complete, though some page-layout text is duplicated/garbled by OCR. Table 2 is titled 'Simulation of the observed values', leaving ambiguity about whether the valve-opening data are field observations or LabVIEW simulation outputs; no water-use measurements, statistics, or dispersion measures are reported anywhere.
